elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.3 lets "A Party ... at any time assign, sell or transfer the whole of its rights and obligations ... to ... a Subsidiary or Affiliate of that Party; and ... another Subsidiary or Affiliate of that Party's Parent Company", and the new subparagraph restricts only "Part[ies] other than Teleglobe USA Inc.", so Customer's consent-free affiliate route survives (22.6 imposes notice only, not consent).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: 22.3(a) permits assignment of the whole of a Party's rights and obligations to "a successor of that Party" without consent, and the insertion expressly excludes Teleglobe USA Inc. from the new consent condition. Noted only: the clause says "successor" without enumerating merger/acquisition/sale-of-substantially-all-assets triggers, a wording shortfall rather than a gap.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted text: "Notwithstanding Paragraph 12 and Subparagraphs 22.2, 22.3, 22.4 and 22.5, no Party other than Teleglobe USA Inc. may assign, sell or transfer the whole or any part of its rights or obligations under this Agreement, including any Transfer under Paragraph 12, without the prior written consent of Teleglobe USA Inc." The notwithstanding language overrides the 22.1 exception routes and reaches partial assignments under 22.4/22.5.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...the prior written consent of Teleglobe USA Inc., which must not be unreasonably withheld."

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and no such assignment, sale or transfer may be made to a competitor of Teleglobe USA Inc." The bar is absolute (not consent-curable) and "no such" ties back to transfers by Parties other than Teleglobe.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "A change of control of Teleglobe USA Inc. does not give any other Party any right to terminate this Agreement or Teleglobe USA Inc.'s participation in it." Declaratory, since no change-of-control exit exists in the cited text; it is nevertheless expressly stated in operative language.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: After the insertion, 22.3(a) remains free only for Teleglobe USA Inc.; every other Party's successor assignment now requires Teleglobe's prior written consent, so the successor right is no longer mutual.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.6: "A Party exercising its rights under Subparagraphs 22.2, 22.3, 22.4 or 22.5 must give notice in writing to all other Parties in a timely manner."
Teleglobe USA Inc. keeps consent-free non-successor routes under 22.3 (Subsidiary/Affiliate/Parent-group), 22.4, 22.5 and Paragraph 12; a retained affiliate exception defeats this element.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: 22.2 ("The Management Committee must not unreasonably withhold or delay its approval") and the inserted "which must not be unreasonably withheld" both carry the reasonableness standard.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements appear in operative language — Customer's consent-free affiliate and successor routes (22.3, subject only to 22.6 notice) are preserved, and the inserted subparagraph supplies (i) a Customer-consent requirement on all other Parties, (ii) a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, (iii) an absolute competitor bar, and (iv) an express no-change-of-control-termination statement.

Fallback level is not met (mutual successor right displaced; Customer retains consent-free affiliate/Paragraph 12 routes), which is acceptable because completeness at either level suffices and curing at fallback would surrender favourable retained 22.3-22.5 rights.

Minimality holds: nothing outside Paragraph 22 and the Paragraph 12 transfer route is altered, no retained favourable language is deleted, and no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedural boilerplate is added. The "including any Transfer under Paragraph 12" extension is defensible rather than an extra because 22.1 itself carves Paragraph 12 out of the no-assignment bar, so leaving it untouched would leave an open route around the new consent requirement — but be prepared to defend it, since 12.13-12.14 are capacity-trading mechanics and other Parties will argue it reaches beyond assignment.

Intent preserved: the "Notwithstanding" opener resolves the tension with retained 22.2-22.5 and Paragraph 12 rather than contradicting them; 22.6 notice, 22.4's Initial Party/voting and Schedule-revision mechanics, and 22.5's cost-allocation conditions all survive intact. The new consent condition is additive to (not a deletion of) the 22.2 Management Committee approval mechanic.

Drafting repairs to make before sending: (1) number the insertion "22.7" in the operative text — the margin comment refers to "new Subparagraph 22.7" but the rendered clause is unnumbered, and 22.1's exception list ("Except as otherwise provided in Paragraph 12 and Subparagraphs 22.2, 22.3, 22.4 and 22.5") should be conformed to read "and subject to Subparagraph 22.7" so the hierarchy is unambiguous on its face; (2) consider defining or qualifying "competitor of Teleglobe USA Inc." (e.g. by reference to carriers competing in identified markets), since the term is presently uncalibrated and invites dispute; (3) if reciprocity is conceded, mirror the clause Party-by-Party rather than deleting our 22.3-22.5 carve-outs, which would drop us below the preferred level.
